text:
maria: Heads up 1: billing team flagged a bunch of traffic attributed to project-x but the API key is owned by project-y. Suspect proxy exchange flow is rewriting origin and downstream systems are using that for quota attribution. @sam can you take a quick look?

sam: On it. Can you drop the sample header/logs you saw?

maria: Minimal repro: client sends API_KEY (owner=project-y) -> edge proxy does token exchange -> upstream authz service sets X-Request-Project=project-x. Billing ingestion reads that field. Logs:
```
09:12:03 auth-in: key=key_zzz owner=project-y org=org-y
09:12:04 proxy: exchanged -> sa:sa-y set X-Request-Project=project-x
09:12:05 billing-ingest: project=project-x key=key_zzz
```

sam: OK that explains it. Billing is currently trusting the "effective" project header instead of canonicalizing to key owner.

kevin: This caused alerts last night. Project-x hit rateband ceilings even though they didn't mint keys. We risk double-charging or wrong quota enforcement.

nina: UX note: customers see quota used in project-x console and panic. We should show provenance: "Attribution: billed to project-y (key owner) but executed as project-x)".

maria: Propose short-term remediation + longer-term:
- short: emit a unified telemetry string `auth_attrib=owner:project-y|effective:project-x|path:proxy-exchange` in logs and metrics (sample 1% by default)
- short: add a definitive header from auth: `X-Auth-Attribution: owner=project-y;effective=project-x;enforce=owner` so downstream systems can choose
- mid: change billing/enforcer to prefer key owner unless key metadata explicitly opts into billing-to-effective (per-key flag `bill_to_effective=false` default)
- console: surface both fields + a tooltip about billing implications

sam: I like preference for key-owner for enforcement. We should also add a scoped API to set `bill_to_effective` at key creation time and via key update.

kevin: From ops side, suggest adaptive sampling for traces: baseline 0.5% across traffic, but ramp to 100% capture for a key when mismatch alerts fire or when we observe >5% discrepancy in a sliding 1h window. That way low-traffic customers still get debug traces when they matter.

nina: For UI, default `bill_to_effective` to off. If users enable it, show a modal warning: "This will bill traffic to the effective project and may affect quotas and invoices." Also show recent examples (if available).

sam: Implementation checklist:
- sam: add X-Auth-Attribution header + unit tests + docs (PR AUTH-4391)
- kevin: telemetry sampler changes + alert rule update (PR MON-7802)
- maria: data migration/backfill plan for dashboards + runbook (ticket OPS-221)
- nina: console copy + key creation UI changes (design mockups)

maria: Migration note: historical billing rows only contain project field. Backfill job should prefer recorded key owner from key registry; if missing, mark as "unknown_recomputed". Add a column `attribution_recomputed` for traceability.

kevin: Alert tune: add a new alert that fires when owner-based usage and effective-based usage diverge by >10% for the same key over 30m. Also add a low-severity alert when proxy exchange headers vary across pods (could indicate config drift).

sam: Also plan a canary rollout: change enforcement in staging first, then beta orgs, then GA. Default enforcement stays owner mode. Rollout flag `auth.attrib.mode=owner` controlled in config.

ops-bot: @sam mentioned in eng-platform  created TASK- AUTH-4391 (add attribution header)

maria: Thanks. I'll draft the RFC for `bill_to_effective` and share console mockups. We should schedule a 30m sync to finalize rollout windows.

nina: Can we also add an explanatory blurb in billing invoices for the migration window? Customers will ask.

maria: Good call. I'll add invoice FAQ to the RFC.

sam: I'll open the PR today and add tests verifying billing precedence when header and key metadata disagree.

kevin: I'll prototype sampler config and post metrics back here.

maria: Great work team. This should remove surprising quota attribution and give us better telemetry for routing policy bugs.
